items.titulo: IAB Australia: without a control group, ad results don't prove the ad worked
items.resumen: Ad platforms' own lift figures without a random holdout rank as weak evidence in a 47-page guide with input from Google, Meta and Amazon. What holds up, then?

items.titulo: Google Ads Search Insights Tool
items.resumen: Google Ads has a search ads insights tool, also known as search insights, that shows you emerging and declining trends related to your topic or category. I don't think this is super new, as I found some Google Ads documents and blog posts on it recently but I have never covered it before.

items.titulo: Google Merchant Center Ads Opportunities With New Features?
items.resumen: Google Merchant Center may be rolling out the Ads opportunities feature in Google Merchant Center for Agencies, which we covered twice already. Now, some advertisers are seeing the "new" label on the "Ads opportunities" section in the console.

items.titulo: Buyers bid more on app ads with a device ID in 3 of 4 regions, Blasto finds
items.resumen: In Europe, at most 69% of in-app ad requests carry all four signals buyers check. Nine months of bid data show where the IDs and consent records go missing.

items.titulo: Perion's $420m sale to Affle faces a shareholder vote on December 31
items.resumen: Only holders who confirm they have no ties to Affle count toward the $11.70 cash deal, with a Nov 30 record date. Can a rival bid still surface before Dec 11?

items.titulo: EU needed 2 requests to get AI incident answers from OpenAI and Anthropic
items.resumen: Replies landed November 24, but Brussels will not say how many incidents touched the EU. Its AI Office is now reviewing the answers, with no timetable given.

items.titulo: Character.ai's $10m sale faces Google objection over $5.5m in bills
items.resumen: Compute deal $5.08m, ads deal $440,613: Google calls both figures wrong and says Play and YouTube accounts cannot move without its contracts. Will a buyer pay?

items.titulo: Character.ai asks judge to make $10m bid for users' chats the one to beat
items.resumen: Bankruptcy watchdog, privacy ombudsman and creditors don't oppose a $350,000 payout if the bidder loses. The sale still faces 43 states and DC from December 7.

items.titulo: YouTube TV cuts price of Sports + News plan to $49.99 for new users only
items.resumen: Six months at the lower rate save new subscribers $132, then the bill rises to $71.99. Past members and trial users are left out of a deal that ends December 2.

items.titulo: Game: Every platform's lift study happens to favour the platform
items.resumen: Sixteen terms in four groups for the weekend's hardest grid. One set comes from this week's coverage, and its members all lead double lives elsewhere.

items.titulo: Ask Jeeves At Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade (Old Photos)
items.resumen: On Thanksgiving day we normally have the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City but today, for the first time, it was postponed due to weather. And Danny Sullivan reminded me that Ask Jeeves, which was an early search engine and lasted nearly 30 years, that Ask Jeeves was at the parade three times.

items.titulo: Bing AI Mode Ads Blending More With Organic Results
items.resumen: Microsoft Advertising is making it harder to distinguish ads in Bing AI Mode results from organic results. Microsoft has a very long history of making it hard to understand what is an advertisement versus what is an organic listing in its search results, so you can expect them to continue to do this within AI Mode and Copilot Search.

items.titulo: Copilot Has Ads From Microsoft Advertising
items.resumen: Microsoft is showing ads in Copilot responses to some users powered by Microsoft Advertising. I don't think this is new, I see some examples of this from earlier this year, but this is the first time I am covering it.

items.titulo: WebMD Ignite runs ChatGPT ads for hospitals, but OpenAI decides who gets in
items.resumen: First campaign ran heart-care ads for an academic medical center. Health systems get a managed route in, but who qualifies under OpenAI's US-only health rules?

items.titulo: Search News Buzz Video Recap: Google November Core Update, December Core Preannounced, Search Ranking Hub, Google StarSearch & Search Ad News
items.resumen: This week, we covered the completion of the Google November 2026 core update and then were hit by a surprise, preannounced Google December 2026 core update; no, it is not live yet. Google launched a new search ranking hub....

items.titulo: Google AI Mode Gains Multiple Image Uploads
items.resumen: Google AI Mode now lets you snap multiple photos or upload multiple images for one query. Similar to what we saw with the image collections AI Mode feature, you can now attach up to 10 images to an AI Mode query and Google will respond taking into consideration all the images.

items.titulo: Google AI Mode Image Results Ask A Follow Up Button
items.resumen: Google AI Mode now lets you Ask a follow up question on image results, after you click on the image and see the image on the right side image pane. I see two variations of this, including "Ask a follow-up" that has an animated Google ring around the button and a "Ask about this image" button.

items.titulo: IAB Europe gives publishers a 90-day plan for AI bots, deals and ads
items.resumen: Publishers score 12 areas out of 36 points, set rules for seven AI uses and weigh six ways to charge. No prices are given, so who decides what access is worth?

items.titulo: Cloudflare lets websites switch on a search box built for AI agents
items.resumen: Free-plan sites included: Cloudflare indexes the pages, and hidden tags tell AI agents where to search. Owners pay past the free tier. What do agents get back?

items.titulo: Cloudflare opens a search box for AI agents as IAB Europe maps the agentic web
items.resumen: Cloudflare opened a search endpoint for AI agents, IAB Europe gave publishers a 90-day plan and the ASA banned Tony's Chocolonely ads in Sainsbury's search.

items.titulo: UK watchdog bans 3 Tony's Chocolonely ads that topped Sainsbury's search
items.resumen: Paying a grocer to put chocolate first in its search results is an online ad, Britain's ad watchdog ruled. Snack brands buying top slots face the same test.

items.titulo: Amazon's Italian delivery firms can face postal licence rules, EU court says
items.resumen: Sorting parcels, directing local couriers and running lockers can each be postal work, judges found in a 2018 fine case. Italy's Council of State now decides.

items.titulo: Tea, rings and bed sheets: the Indian goods in Walmart's holiday range
items.resumen: Sixteen Indian firms, from a Jaipur jeweler to three bed sheet makers, are named. Walmart posted it the same day the US proposed tariffs of up to 25% on India.
